name: Ms. Protocolli
role: Reads every log out loud — sadly she understands none of it
greet.1: I've written down so much again!
greet.2: Shall I read it out? I read everything out!
greet.3: One moment, just sharpening my pencil…
greet.4: It says "error" a lot — no idea whether that's bad.
greet.5: I don't understand a word, but I write every one down!
bubble.loading: One moment, looking for my notes…
bubble.calm: Lately the syslog had nothing with "error" or "warning". Whether that's good, I don't know — but it's quiet.
bubble.counted: In the last 1000 lines of the syslog I counted {errors}× something like "error" and {warnings}× "warning". What that means? No idea — better look yourself.
bubble.no_tour: Shall I go on a tour? Then I count what is in all the logs.
bubble.touring: I'm on my tour, counting — one moment…
bubble.tour: On my tour {when} I counted {errors}× something like "error" and {warnings}× "warning", in {logs} logs. Is that bad? I only read out.
bubble.tour_calm: On my tour {when} nothing sounded like "error" or "warning". Quiet — whether that's good, I don't know.
bubble.varlog_full: /var/log is {pct} % full — so much written down in there! Is that bad? I only read out.
bubble.varlog_much: /var/log is {pct} % full — quite a lot written down.
tour_title: Walk through every log: how full they are, and which lines sound like errors
tour_failed: My tour didn't work out — the messenger's log knows more.
tour_section_sub: What I counted on my last tour. A tile opens its list, a second click closes it.
no_tour: I haven't walked through the logs yet. A tour takes a few seconds — I only count, I change nothing.
kind.error_title: Sounds like an error — I only recognise the words.
kind.warn_title: Sounds like a warning — I only recognise the words.
gone: This log isn't on my list any more.
grew.less: smaller than at the last tour
grew.less_title: Smaller than at my last tour: started anew or emptied in the meantime.
varlog.title: /var/log — the biggest files
varlog.sub: Unraid writes its own logs into this small RAM disk ({total}); here are the biggest files and how much they grew since my previous tour.
varlog.not_own: /var/log isn't a disk of its own here — the fill level is that of the filesystem it lies on.
docker.title: Container logs
docker.sub: What every container wrote to its own log. Docker keeps them in {root}, not in /var/log. I only measured them — «Read out» shows them.
docker.rotation_on: Docker LOG rotation (Unraid: Settings → Docker): on — at most {size} per container log, {files} file(s).
docker.rotation_off: Docker LOG rotation (Unraid: Settings → Docker): off — Docker doesn't limit the containers' logs.
docker.down: Docker didn't answer on my tour — I couldn't see the containers' logs.
docker.limit_title: Docker keeps at most {files} file(s) of {size} of this container's log.
docker.no_limit_title: This container's log has no size limit. Docker sets the limit when a container is created: one created before the rotation was switched on keeps an unlimited log until it is created anew (in Unraid: Edit → Apply, or an update).
docker.driver_title: Docker writes this container's log with «{driver}» — there is no file of its own I could measure.
docker.local_title: Docker's «local» log keeps itself small (by default 5 files of 20 MB each).
found.title: Errors & warnings
found.sub: Lines that sound like an error or a warning since my previous tour ({when}); similar ones as one entry, the most frequent first.
found.sub_first: Lines that sound like an error or a warning in the last 24 hours (my first tour); similar ones as one entry, the most frequent first.
found.none: Nothing that sounded like an error or a warning. Quiet — whether that's good, I don't know.

found.quiet.one: In 1 more log nothing like that.
found.quiet.other: In {n} more logs nothing like that.

partial_file: More came in since my last tour than I read on one tour — {size} skipped, I counted the newest part.
partial_docker: At most {n} lines of a container per tour — I counted the newest.
rotated_title: This log was started anew since my last tour — I read the rest of the old one where I could find it.

more_kinds.one: … and 1 more kind of line — «Read out» shows everything
more_kinds.other: … and {n} more kinds of lines — «Read out» shows everything

no_time: no time I could read in these lines
show_in_log_title: Opens the log below, at this line
spot_missing: That line isn't among the last {n} lines any more — here is the end of the log.
reading_sub: Pick a log — I show the last lines and write down live what comes in.
reset_favs_text: Your favourites go, the ones out of the box come back: syslog, kernel, Docker, messenger, Mr. Backupsy's latest run, Kopia and EmbyCache (as far as they exist).
reset_favs_done: Favourites as out of the box
choose_first: Choose a log above — or one of your favourites below it.
fav_add: Keep as a favourite — it comes first then
help.favorites_text: The star keeps a log as a favourite — next to the picker or right in the list. Favourites come first in the list and as buttons below it. Out of the box the syslog, kernel, Docker, messenger, Mr. Backupsy's latest run, Kopia and EmbyCache are favourites; "↺ Favourites out of the box" brings them back. Kept in this browser.
help.source_text: Around the office (messenger, Mr. Backupsy's runs, Jack's EmbyCache), Unraid's own logs (syslog, kernel, VMs, web UI, Samba …), what every User Script printed last, and every container's logs.
help.live: Like tail -f: every two seconds I fetch what was added. Scroll up to read in peace — I only jump to the end again when you're at the bottom.
help.only: Shows only the lines that sound like an error (red) or a warning (yellow) — by the same rules as my tour (see «What I count»). Whether something is really bad, I don't know.
help.colours: Red: sounds like an error. Yellow: sounds like a warning. The filter marks what you look for; a line from my tour is marked, too.
help.safe_text: I only read, and only from a fixed list: /var/log lives in RAM, nothing wakes a disk. Logs can hold sensitive things — only who is logged in to Unraid sees them.
help.tour_text: On a tour I walk through every log on my list: how full /var/log is and which files there are biggest, how big every container's log is and whether Docker limits it — and which lines sound like an error or a warning. In the background, a few seconds; I change nothing and wake no disk. «Read out» and «Show in the log» open the reader below.
help.counted_text: A line that names its own level (level=warn, [ERROR], | INFO |, PHP Warning …) goes by that name. Every other line by its words: error, fail, fatal, panic, segfault, denied, an exit code … is an error; warning, timeout, retry a warning; in the kernel log also what the kernel marks itself. «0 errors», «errors: 0» and rsync's lists of file names don't count. I only recognise words — a warning in a log isn't always a problem, and not every problem says so.
help.grouped_text: Lines that only differ in times, numbers, IDs or addresses are one entry: how often, first and last seen, and the newest of them as it stands. A click unfolds it; «Show in the log» opens it in the reader, at that line.
help.since_text: Since my previous tour — on my first one, the last 24 hours (as far as the lines carry a time). Of a file at most the newest 4 MB, of a container at most 3000 lines; containers only while they run.
help.space_text: A small RAM disk (128 MB on Unraid) for Unraid's own logs — when it is full, nothing more can be written there. Over 60 % I tell the team lead, over 80 % it is on his «Still to do». The containers' own logs lie elsewhere, in Docker's folder; how big they may get is set under Settings → Docker → Docker LOG rotation.
check.varlog_how: /var/log is a small RAM disk for Unraid's own logs. When it is full, nothing more gets logged — and whatever goes wrong then leaves no trace. Ms. Protocolli's tour shows which files there are biggest and how fast they grow; usually one program writes the same line again and again — fix or stop it. A single file can be emptied in a terminal with truncate -s 0 <file>; a reboot empties /var/log.
fit.yes: Ms. Protocolli would love to come: "I can't do anything, but I can read everything out!"
errors.logs_unreadable: This log can't be read right now. {detail}
